title: Distinct variable indices in an AND clause
statement: Fix $n$, and let $lits$ be a list of literals over the variables $\{0,\dots,n-1\}$ whose underlying variable indices, obtained by taking the index of each literal in $lits$, are pairwise distinct. If a normal-form AND circuit on $n$ variables equals the base clause built from $lits$ together with this distinctness witness, then the list of variable indices of $lits$ has no repeated entries.
hypotheses_covered: the variable indices of lits are pairwise distinct (Nodup)
the circuit c equals the clause built from lits and this distinctness proof
replaced:
If a normal-form AND circuit $c$ equals a clause built from literals $lits$ with a
duplication-free proof $h$, then the variable indices $lits.\mathrm{map}\;\mathrm{Lit.idx}$
are pairwise distinct.
